extracted.intended_audience: beginner improvisers / prospective students looking for an introductory improv class (adults)
extracted.subtask_description: An introductory, in-person improv course teaching foundational improvisational principles and skills — centered on 'Yes, And', ensemble work, listening, spontaneity, and risk-taking — delivered through group exercises and games.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yes, And
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement the concept of "Yes, And" to foster collaboration and creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The class emphasizes the fundamental concept of “Yes, And” in improvisation; students are expected to make and accept offers, build on partners' ideas, and use the technique to create forward-moving scenes and collaborative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble-based teamwork
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will use teamwork to generate ideas and support ensemble members in improv scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on supporting ensemble members rather than individual spotlighting; generate ideas collectively and sustain scenes as a group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impulse & spontaneity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises and games are designed to surface quick, instinctive responses; learners should practice trusting impulses to create fresh, surprising material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listening
rubrics_metrics.description: Listening as a core skill for improvisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay close attention to scene partners' offers and details so you can respond honestly and build the scene; effective listening enables appropriate accepts and extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being present in the moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Being present in the moment while performing improv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stay focused on the current scene and inputs rather than planning ahead; presence supports spontaneity, truthful reactions, and ensemble responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking risks / Risk taking
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will explore taking risks in game settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course encourages risk-taking as a way to discover new material; the environment is framed to allow failing joyfully and learning from daring choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding agreement / Making & accepting offers
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding agreement (making & accepting offers) to move scenes forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice the mechanics of making clear offers and accepting others' offers to create shared reality and momentum in scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication / Effective communication skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Through improv games and exercises students will learn to enhance effective communication skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use improv practice to develop verbal and nonverbal communication, clarity of intention, and responsiveness that transfer to everyday interactions and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive environment / Trust and failing joyfully
rubrics_metrics.description: A supportive environment that embraces the idea of trusting yourself and failing joyfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The class setting is explicitly supportive to encourage experimentation; instructors expect students to take creative risks without fear of judgment and to view mistakes as learning opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice through group exercises and games
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of group exercises and games as the primary training method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skills are developed experientially via structured games and exercises rather than lecture; consistent participation in these exercises is implied to build improv fundamentals.
